subject: Clarifying CCPA/CPRA service-provider scope and subprocessor transfers
messages:
From: Samantha Rogers <samantha@privsecure.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: PrivSecure Legal <legal@privsecure.io>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: CCPA/CPRA scope — are you a service provider only?

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo today. A quick legal check from our privacy team: we need to confirm that Redwood will act as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and will not "sell" personal information. Two follow-ups from our side:

1) Please confirm whether Redwood processes any segment of our customer data that could be interpreted as a "sale" (e.g., third-party ad targeting, enrichment, or marketplace telemetry sharing).
2) We also need a current list of subprocessors and an indication of which subprocessors may transfer data outside the US (specifically EU/Canada). Our procurement team will attach a redline to your DPA.

Can you provide both items by end of week? We attached a short questionnaire earlier — happy to walk through it.

Regards,
Samantha Rogers
Director, Privacy & Compliance
PrivSecure, Inc.

Attachment: subprocessors_request_template.pdf (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Rogers <samantha@privsecure.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 17:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA scope — are you a service provider only?

Samantha —

Thanks for the note and for flagging. Short answers up front:
- Redwood confirms we operate as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA for customers who specify Redwood as their processor/service provider; we do not sell personal information as part of our hosted inference service or Dedicated deployments.
- We do run a small set of telemetry/operational events for platform health (latency/error traces) — these are aggregated and used for reliability and billing; they are not used for advertising.

That said, I'll loop in Legal and Ops to give you a redline and a current subprocessor snapshot. Attached is our proposed redline to a standard DPA (see file "Redline_Data_Processing_Addendum_20261203.docx") and a current subprocessor export ("subprocessors_snapshot_20261130.csv").

Action items:
- Neha (Legal) — can you review the redline and confirm the CPRA service-provider language and transfer mechanism (SCCs / other)
- Priyom (Infra) — will review subprocessor list to confirm which vendors process outside the US.

I can set up a quick call if PrivSecure wants to walk through the redline.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance (redwood inference)

Attachments: Redline_Data_Processing_Addendum_20261203.docx (redline stub), subprocessors_snapshot_20261130.csv (stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA scope — are you a service provider only?

Looping in a few clarifications from Legal:

Marcus — quick points for the PrivSecure thread before we send a formal reply:
- Confirm the "no sale" statement in plain language in the DPA redline (we should add a short clause: "Redwood does not sell, disclose for cross-context behavioral advertising, or otherwise make available Personal Information to third parties except as directed by Customer or as required by law.").
- For CPRA-specific requirements (opt-out mechanisms, purpose limitation), propose we reference an Appendix: "CPRA Addendum" that mirrors our standard service-provider obligations and excludes any advertising use.
- Subprocessor transfers: we should state which subprocessors are covered by SCCs or rely on adequacy decisions. Priyom, please mark which vendors export to EU/Canada and whether they have SCCs in place.

Samantha — we'll send a redline with the extra clause and a clearer subprocessor transfer statement by EOD PST. If PrivSecure requires additional evidence (SOC 2 report or flow diagrams), let us know and we'll provide the document links.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:11:00 -08:00

Hi Marcus / Neha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying asks from PrivSecure Legal:
- Can you explicitly state in the DPA redline that Redwood will not use our data for product development or model training unless we opt in? (We need a clear prohibition unless there is an explicit clause.)
- For subprocessors that process telemetry in EU/Canada: does Redwood act as the data exporter for SCCs, or will the subprocessors rely on their own SCC arrangements? Our procurement team needs to map responsibility for signing/maintaining SCCs.

Also attaching our procurement team's redline to the DPA for reference — they moved a few clauses. If you can send a consolidated redline that addresses the training prohibition and the SCC ownership model, that would help.

Thanks,
Samantha

Attachment: PrivSecure_DPA_redline_20261129.pdf (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Rogers <samantha@privsecure.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA scope — are you a service provider only?

Samantha —

Thanks — we reviewed your points and prepared a consolidated response: see attached redline (Redline_Data_Processing_Addendum_20261203.docx). High-level answers here: 

1) No-training/derivative use: we will add an explicit clause to the DPA and CPRA addendum: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve or retrain models, build features, or for product development unless Customer provides prior written consent." That addresses your procurement team's concern.

2) SCCs and subprocessors: Redwood's model is that the Customer (PrivSecure) is the data exporter for SCC purposes when data is exported from the EEA/UK; Redwood will support and execute standard SCC templates as necessary for our vendor-to-vendor data flows. For subprocessors that independently act as exporters, we require SCCs between Redwood and that subprocessors; Priyom has flagged which vendors process outside the US and their SCC status in the attached CSV.

Next steps:
- Neha will finalize the CPRA addendum clause and return a consolidated DPA redline.
- Priyom will confirm SCC execution status for the listed subprocessors and follow up if any require remedial steps.
- Marcus to schedule a 30-min call if PrivSecure wants to review final redline.

If that works, reply with preferred times and we'll lock the call.

Best,
Marcus
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
